(1) the performance of convolution codes over non-stationaly noise channel can be analyzed by considering the instantaneous or the time-average noise power, (2) the instantaneous power is the best choice when the noise power is highly variable (e.g., heavy-tailed distributions), (3) the performance of codes is degraded by a factor of 2-3dB with respect to the AWGN case, (4) the degradation depends on the noise power distribution, (5) the performance of

the average error probability of convolutional codes is affected by the interference scenario, and that the performance of the codes can be improved by using a decoder with knowledge of the noise power.
Convolutional coding with interleaving is a very effective way to combat the effects of time-varying noise.

the performance of convolution codes with bit interleaver in the presence of time-varying noise, and it can be used to design a robust communication system for the non-stationarity noise channel.
the performance of convolution codes in presence of non-Gaussian noise with non-stationary statistics, such as interference from co-channel users, multipath propagation or fading channels.
the design of a new class of convolutional codes, called quasi-cyclic codes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of convolutionally coded systems over non-stationnary-noise channel can be improved if the receiver is aware of the instantaneous interference power.
the performance of convolutionally encoded bit interleaved systems can be greatly improved by exploiting instantaneous noise power information, even in presence of nonstationary noise.
the performance gain in the presence of non-stable interference can be significant and it is strongly dependent on the knowledge of instantaneous or average noise power.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in presence of non-Gaussian interference, the knowledge of the channel state information at the receiver is crucial to achieve the best possible performance.
the knowledge of the average interference power at the receiver can be sufficient to achieve near-optimal error performance in presence of nonstationary noise.
the proposed analytical framework can be used as a design tool for convolutional codes with interleaving in the presence of non-stable interference.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the interference is not Gaussian distributed, the performance of the receiver is improved if the instantaneous noise power is used for the decoding process.

the knowledge of the average noise power is sufficient to achieve near-optimal performance in the presence of non-stochastic noise, while the knowledge of the exact instantaneous noise power is required for stochastic noise.
the performance of the convolutional codes is significantly affected by the knowledge of the noise statistics at the receiver.
